Paragraph: Summary of Passage: Actions do not taint Krishna because He has no desire for the fruits of action; understanding this principle frees individuals from the binding karma of work.
Situation/Problem_Faced: How to engage in active work without accumulating psychological baggage or karmic entanglement.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna states: 'na mam karmani limpanti na me karma-phale sprha, iti mam yo 'bhijanati karmabhir na sa badhyate' (Work does not affect Me, nor do I desire action's fruits; one who knows Me thus is not bound by karma).
Outcome/Resolution: Provides the blueprint for Karma-yoga: acting without selfish desire prevents psychological entanglement.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Freedom from Outcome Attachment: Working dedicatedly without obsessing over personal reward
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Unbiased Action: Performing duty cleanly without personal bias or ulterior motives
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Preventing Psychological Burnout: Avoiding emotional exhaustion by releasing control over final results

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Na mam karmani limpanti (Actions do not taint or bind Me)
Na me karma-phale sprha (I have no longing for the fruits of action)
Karmabhir na sa badhyate (Such a person is not bound by karma)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The Supreme Lord remains untainted by creation because He has no desire for results; comprehending this detachment frees seekers from karmic bondage.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Working without egoic attachment to outcomes protects mental health, preventing anxiety and stress while maintaining high-quality effort.
